route_name: Per-vertex free-probability growth: the pointwise lemma PV is dead in the window; the live target is its closed-neighbourhood average R1
target_lemma:
EXACT REDUCTION (elementary, asserted in code at every level of every tree touched). This holds for every forest T and k>=1. Put G_v=T-N[v], j^v_k=i_k(G_v), and pi_k(v)=j^v_k/i_k(T)=P_k(v free), so sum_v pi_k(v)=mu_k. Two double counts give k i_k(T)=sum_v i_{k-1}(G_v) and (k+1) i_{k+1}(T)=sum_v i_k(G_v). The second is Fang et al. (8.1), p.14, written vertex by vertex. Define
D_v(k) := k i_{k-1}(T) j^v_k - (k+1) i_k(T) j^v_{k-1} = k i_{k-1} i_k [pi_k(v) - (1+1/k) pi_{k-1}(v)].
Then sum_v D_v(k) = k(k+1)(i_{k-1} i_{k+1} - i_k^2). So LC at k, equivalently mu_k <= (1+1/k) mu_{k-1}, is exactly sum_v D_v(k) <= 0. As a Turan/Newton pair count, take Q1={(S,u,v,S')} (S,S' in I_{k-1}, (u,v) an ordered non-adjacent free pair of S) and Q2={(S,u,S',v)}. LC is |Q1| <= (1+1/k)|Q2|. The identity map is defined on Q1 exactly when v is also free for S'. Its defect, summed by the marked vertex v, is sum_v D_v.

LEMMA PV (pointwise; DEAD). For every tree T on n vertices, every vertex v, and every k with ceil(n/4) <= k <= q := ceil((2 alpha-1)/3): k i_{k-1}(T) i_k(T-N[v]) <= (k+1) i_k(T) i_{k-1}(T-N[v]). Equivalently P_k(v free) <= (1+1/k) P_{k-1}(v free). The no-slack form (PV0) sums to Mason (b). It is parked and was recorded only as a diagnostic.

LEMMA R1 (live target; survives every test run). For every tree T on n vertices, every k in [ceil(n/4), q], and every vertex u: L_u(k) := sum_{v in N[u]} D_v(k)/(deg v + 1) <= 0. Equivalently, for the weighted local free count F~_u(S) = sum_{v in N[u]} 1[v free for S]/(deg v+1), E_k[F~_u] <= (1+1/k) E_{k-1}[F~_u]. Since sum_u L_u = sum_v D_v (partition of unity), R1 implies LC at k. No constants beyond the slack 1/k and the window endpoints. The weaker edge average R2 (D_a/deg a + D_b/deg b <= 0 on every edge) is dead.
how_it_closes:
Suppose PV or R1 held on [ceil(n/4), q]. Then LC holds at every k in [ceil(n/4), q], so r_k = i_{k+1}/i_k is nonincreasing on [ceil(n/4)-1, q]. Fang Prop 8.2 (statement p.15, proof p.16, from (k+1)i_{k+1}/i_k >= n-3k) gives i_0 <= ... <= i_{ceil(n/4)}, that is r_k >= 1 for k <= ceil(n/4)-1. The bipartite Levit-Mandrescu tail ((8.9), p.15; proof p.16 via e(J) <= 2(alpha-k)) gives r_k <= 1 for k >= q. So r crosses 1 at most once and the sequence is unimodal.

The window is never empty. Because alpha >= ceil(n/2) for forests, q >= ceil((n-1)/3) >= ceil(n/4) for n >= 4. This was also checked directly for alpha = ceil(n/2) at every n <= 5000, and K1 found no tree n <= 18 with an empty window.

So a deterministic proof gives N1 = 1: unimodality for every tree (and forest, since the identities, Prop 8.2 and the tail all hold for forests) with no size threshold. The exhaustive n <= 32 record would become redundant rather than load-bearing. Caveat: PV and R1 were tested on trees only. No such proof exists yet. The route contributes no effective N1 unless R1, or another aggregate, is proved.

Prop 8.2 prefix and the Levit-Mandrescu tail close the argument. (8.1) is the second double count.

That lane wanted I(T-r) ratio-dominating I(T-N[r]) with no slack, at support vertices, over the whole prefix, and SCC died at n=28. PV needs slack 1/k, every vertex, and the window only. Through the mediant I(T)=I(T-v)+x I(T-N[v]), PV follows from (a) ratio dominance with slack at v plus (b) weak LC of T-N[v] at k-1. On n<=18, (a) fails 304 times (first at n=6) where PV still holds, while (b) never fails. So the old ratio-dominance mechanism is lossy here, and R1 is that program with slack and averaging added. It is not a new mechanism.

kill_test:
K1 (first executable kill-test). For every tree 4<=n<=18 (gentreeg -p), every vertex v and every k in [ceil(n/4), q], test D_v(k) <= 0 by exact integer cross-multiplication. Also test every k in [1, alpha] to locate where PV first fails. Diagnostic columns: PV0 (no slack), the mediant pieces (a) ratio dominance with slack and (b) weak LC of T-N[v], and the max PV ratio.

Kill criterion: any D_v(k) > 0 inside the window while LC holds kills the pointwise lemma. Any L_u(k) > 0 inside the window while LC holds kills R1, and the same for R2.

Follow-ups, all exact:
- K2: the 1,228 LC-failing census trees (28<=n<=32), at the window, k=alpha-1 and k=alpha-2.
- K3/K5/K6: adversarial families to n=141 (hub-stars H(m,t), mason bouquets, SCC brooms, double stars, caterpillars, spiders, hubs with extra leaves/tails/mixed arms, two adjacent hubs, hubs of hubs, stars of hubs).
- K4: hill-climbs (leaf moves, leaf add/remove), with every hit re-checked exactly.
- Independent brute-force recount (bitmask branching, no tree DP) of the counterexample.
kill_test_result:
K1, all 205,001 trees 4<=n<=18, 11,831,916 (v,k) window checks: 0 PV failures and 0 PV0 failures on the window. PV also has 0 failures at any k in [1,alpha]. LC holds everywhere. The max PV ratio in the window climbs with n: 107/133=0.805 (n=13), 937/1080=0.868 (n=16), 8648/9765=0.886 (n=18). The worst vertex is always the hub of a hub-star at k=q. Mediant diagnostics: (b) 0 failures; (a) 304 failures (first at n=6); implication (a)+(b)=>PV 0 violations.

K3, the kill criterion fired: pointwise PV is FALSE in the window. Hub-star H(9,2) (hub joined to 9 vertices each carrying 2 leaves), n=28, alpha=19, window [7,13], v=hub:
- k=12: D_v = +23,677,056, PV ratio 327243/327119.
- k=13: D_v = +301,182,336, ratio 75489/74137.
LC holds there (margins 4,970,084,760 and 855,779,832). Recomputed independently by bitmask branching (data/counterexample_recheck_bruteforce.txt). This is a constant-factor violation: the ratio reaches 1.15 for H(m,2) at m~24 (n=73) and stays there. It also fails below the mode: H(16,4) (n=81, mode 32) fails PV at k=26..31, and PV0 fails from k=17 < ceil(n/4)=21. PV failed in the window in 41 of 272 K3 members and 147 of 303 K5/K6 members (n up to 141). Every failing vertex found has degree 9 to 37 (hubs only). Mechanism, exact for H(m,2) and checked with Fractions at lambda in {1/2,1,2,3}: P_lambda(hub free) = 1/(g(lambda)^m + lambda), g = 1 + lambda/(1+lambda)^2. Since g is decreasing for lambda > 1, the hub's free probability rises with density there (m=9: 0.118 at lambda=1, 0.130 at lambda=3). Fang's window uses lambda up to 12 (p.3).

K2, 1,228 LC-failing census trees:
- Windows (5,113 levels): 0 PV failures.
- k=alpha-1, where LC fails in all 1,228: 14 to 19 PV-failing vertices per tree. Of the 20,651 failing instances, 13,950 are leaves and 2,437 have degree 2. The failures are never confined to max-degree vertices, and R1 fails in all 1,228, as it must.
- k=alpha-2: 0 PV failures.

K5/K6, repairs:
- R1: 0 failures on all 450 family trees (147 with pointwise PV failures). The worst normalised load among PV-failing trees is -0.19 × mean|D_v|.
- R2: dead (two hubs H(12,2) joined hub-to-hub, n=74; also n=92, 122).

K4, hill-climbs:
- PV: 79,133 evaluations over 19<=n<=27, 0 violations, optimum 0.983 at H(8,2), n=25. This is not evidence that 28 is minimal.
- R1: 46,492 evaluations over 20<=n<=50, 0 violations, best load -0.21 (a weaker adversary than the families, whose worst was -0.099).

main_obstacle:
1. First-order counting provably cannot reach the window. The deterministic facts in hand bound mu, not its slope: Fang Lemma 8.1 (mu_{k-1} >= n-3(k-1)), the tail bound mu_k <= 2(alpha-k), and identity (3) of the Mason note. Combined, they certify LC at k only when 2k(alpha-k) <= (k+1)(n-3k+3). For alpha=n/2 this reduces exactly to k^2 <= n+3, far below ceil(n/4). LC and PV are curvature statements.

2. The natural injection and local lemma PV is false by a constant factor inside the window. First counterexample is the hub-star H(9,2), n=28; the violation reaches 1.15. It also fails below the mode (H(16,4), n=81). So neither the 1/k slack nor restricting to the ascending part rescues it. The cause is hubs whose freeness is aligned with maximum-type configurations ('S lies in the leaves'). Defect must therefore be moved between neighbouring vertices.

3. The window restriction is essential, and the census shows where. At k=alpha-1 the positive defect is spread over 14 to 19 mostly low-degree vertices (two-thirds of them leaves), so no small-neighbourhood average survives. In the window only hubs fail, and R1 absorbs them. A proof would have to use k <= q exactly to stop leaves' free probabilities from jumping by more than 1+1/k. I have no step that does this.

4. The surviving R1 has no proof mechanism. It compares the ratio sequence of T with those of the forests T-N[v], v in N[u], at a single level. That is the ratio-dominance / Condition C program (SCC dead at n=28) with slack and averaging added. Its mediant component (a) is already lossy (it fails at n=6 where PV holds). The inductive piece (b), weak LC of T-N[v] at k-1, can land above that smaller forest's own window when v is a hub, which is exactly where LC breaks. Nothing in the free-count double counts controls such cross-forest ratio comparisons.
